newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Flood waters rise on Hungarian stretch of Danube.
newsitem.headline: Flood waters rise on Hungarian stretch of Danube.

text.p: Water levels along the Hungarian section of the river Danube rose steadily on Sunday, with low level flood warnings issued for the towns of Komarom, Esztergom, Dunaremete and Rajka.

Hungary's Flood Control Centre told Hungarian news agency MTI the current 562 centimetre level of the Danube at Budapest was expected to rise by a daily 70 centimetres on Monday and Tuesday and will peak at 710 centimetres on Wednesday.
Such a level poses no threat of flooding to the capital.
The Centre said there was no rise in water levels along Hungary's second largest river in the east of the country, the Tisza.
Danube shipping was suspended in Austria on Sunday as days of torrential rain took their toll.
The river, which flows from the Alps to the Black Sea, was closed to traffic along a 90 km (50 mile) stretch between Linz and Krems, state television reported.

Hungarian Civil Guard spokeswoman Julianna Osz-Biro told MTI a Hungarian rescue team had arrived on Sunday in the Polish city of Wroclaw with ten high capacity pumps provided by the Hungarian government.
A previous team arrived on Wroclaw on Friday and started up the water purification installation that supplies the city"s hospital, she said.
Osz-Biro added Hungary will also deliver 25 tonnes of disinfectant to Poland in the first half of the week.
Hungary's government decided on Thursday to offer Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia 350 million forints ($1.8 million) in aid to relieve the effects of current floods in the region.
